### Parameter catalogue

This step prepares a clean catalogue of IMPC parameters from `IMPC_parameter_description`. It keeps the parameter ID and name, standardises their column names for later use, removes rows with missing identifiers or names, and removes duplicate ID–name pairs. This catalogue is the reference used to build the parameter groups.

```{r}
if ("parameterId" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description)) {
  parameter_id_column <- "parameterId"
} else if ("parameter_id" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description)) {
  parameter_id_column <- "parameter_id"
} else {
  stop("No parameter ID column was found.")
}

if ("name" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description)) {
  parameter_name_column <- "name"
} else if ("parameter_name" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description)) {
  parameter_name_column <- "parameter_name"
} else {
  stop("No parameter name column was found.")
}

parameter_catalog <- data.frame(
  parameter_id = as.character(
    IMPC_parameter_description[[parameter_id_column]]
  ),
  parameter_name = as.character(
    IMPC_parameter_description[[parameter_name_column]]
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

parameter_catalog$parameter_id <- trimws(parameter_catalog$parameter_id)
parameter_catalog$parameter_name <- trimws(parameter_catalog$parameter_name)

parameter_catalog <- parameter_catalog[
  !is.na(parameter_catalog$parameter_id) &
    parameter_catalog$parameter_id != "" &
    !is.na(parameter_catalog$parameter_name) &
    parameter_catalog$parameter_name != "",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

parameter_catalog <- unique(parameter_catalog)
rownames(parameter_catalog) <- NULL
```

### Parameter_group helper function

This step defines a reusable function for selecting parameters by keywords in their names. It adds the requested group name to each selected parameter, so the same selection logic can be reused for several groups.

```{r}
make_group <- function(pattern, group_label) {
  selected <- parameter_catalog[
    grepl(
      pattern,
      parameter_catalog$parameter_name,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  
  selected$group_name <- group_label
  selected
}
```

### Images group

This step creates the Images group using the seven parameter IDs selected for image-related measurements. It also checks whether any of those IDs are missing from the parameter catalogue, so they can be reviewed before the group is used.

```{r}
image_ids <- c(
  "IMPC_EYE_050_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_072_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_073_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_074_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_075_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_078_001",
  "IMPC_EYE_079_001"
)

image_group_members <- parameter_catalog[
  parameter_catalog$parameter_id %in% image_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

image_group_members$group_name <- "Images"

image_ids_not_found <- setdiff(
  image_ids,
  parameter_catalog$parameter_id
)

image_ids_not_found
```

### Weight group

This step selects parameters whose names suggest that they relate to body weight or body mass. It then excludes specified parameters, such as grip-strength and experimental-effect measures, that should not be classified as weight parameters.

```{r}
weight_group_members <- make_group(
  "body weight|body mass|bodyweight|weight gain|weight loss",
  "Weight"
)

exclude_weight_ids <- c(
  "IMPC_GRS_010_001",
  "IMPC_GRS_011_001",
  "IMPC_EXD_016_001",
  "IMPC_EXD_047_001",
  "IMPC_EXD_069_001",
  "IMPC_EXD_099_001"
)

weight_group_members <- weight_group_members[
  !weight_group_members$parameter_id %in% exclude_weight_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

### Brain group

This step selects parameters whose names refer to the brain or brain regions. It excludes “renal cortex,” because that term refers to the kidney rather than the brain.

```{r}
brain_group_members <- make_group(
  "brain|cerebell|hippocamp|cortex",
  "Brain"
)

brain_group_members <- brain_group_members[
  !grepl(
    "renal cortex",
    brain_group_members$parameter_name,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

### Haematology and immunophenotyping group

This step selects parameters whose names contain keywords related to blood, blood cells, or haematology. The selected parameters are assigned to the `Haematology_and_immunophenotyping` group.

```{r}
haematology_group_members <- make_group(
  "haemat|hemat|platelet|erythrocyte|leukocyte|haemoglobin|hemoglobin|blood cell",
  "Haematology_and_immunophenotyping"
)
```

### Behaviour group

This step selects parameters whose names suggest behavioural or activity-related measurements, including locomotion, grip strength, startle response, anxiety, learning, and memory.

```{r}
behaviour_group_members <- make_group(
  "behavio|activity|locomot|grip|startle|anxiety|learning|memory",
  "Behaviour"
)
```

### Clinical chemistry and metabolism group

This step selects parameters whose names suggest clinical chemistry or metabolism, including glucose, insulin, cholesterol, enzymes, creatinine, and urea.

```{r}
clinical_chemistry_group_members <- make_group(
  "glucose|insulin|cholesterol|triglyceride|bilirubin|enzyme|metabol|chemistry|creatinine|urea",
  "Clinical_chemistry_and_metabolism"
)
```

### Combined parameter_group candidates

This step removes experimental-design and quality-control parameters from the phenotype groups, and removes reagent-information parameters from the clinical chemistry group. It then combines the selected parameters into one candidate table and counts the unique parameters in each group. These are candidate assignments and should be reviewed before being used as final group membership data.

```{r}
# Remove experimental-design and quality-control parameters from phenotype groups
remove_non_phenotype_parameters <- function(x) {
  x[
    !grepl(
      "^(Blinding|Instrumentation effects|Operator effects|Order effects)",
      x$parameter_name,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}

weight_group_members <- remove_non_phenotype_parameters(weight_group_members)
brain_group_members <- remove_non_phenotype_parameters(brain_group_members)
haematology_group_members <- remove_non_phenotype_parameters(haematology_group_members)
behaviour_group_members <- remove_non_phenotype_parameters(behaviour_group_members)
clinical_chemistry_group_members <- remove_non_phenotype_parameters(
  clinical_chemistry_group_members
)

# Remove reagent-information parameters from Clinical chemistry and metabolism
clinical_chemistry_group_members <- clinical_chemistry_group_members[
  !grepl(
    "^Enzyme buffer (manufacturer|catalog number)$",
    clinical_chemistry_group_members$parameter_name,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Rebuild the combined candidate table
parameter_group_candidates <- unique(
  rbind(
    image_group_members,
    weight_group_members,
    brain_group_members,
    haematology_group_members,
    behaviour_group_members,
    clinical_chemistry_group_members
  )
)

rownames(parameter_group_candidates) <- NULL

# Recalculate the number of candidate parameters in each group
group_counts <- aggregate(
  parameter_id ~ group_name,
  data = parameter_group_candidates,
  FUN = function(x) length(unique(x))
)

names(group_counts)[2] <- "candidate_parameter_count"

knitr::kable(group_counts)
```

### Check group assignments

This step checks whether the same parameter–group assignment appears more than once and whether any parameter has been assigned to multiple groups. These checks help identify duplicate or overlapping assignments for review.

```{r}
# Find repeated parameter-to-group assignments
duplicate_memberships <- parameter_group_candidates[
  duplicated(parameter_group_candidates[c("parameter_id", "group_name")]) |
    duplicated(
      parameter_group_candidates[c("parameter_id", "group_name")],
      fromLast = TRUE
    ),
]

View(duplicate_memberships)
# Check whether any parameter ID is assigned to multiple groups
groups_per_parameter <- aggregate(
  group_name ~ parameter_id,
  data = unique(parameter_group_candidates[c("parameter_id", "group_name")]),
  FUN = function(x) paste(sort(unique(x)), collapse = ", ")
)

multiple_group_assignments <- groups_per_parameter[
  grepl(",", groups_per_parameter$group_name, fixed = TRUE),
]

View(multiple_group_assignments)
```

### Create the parameter_group and parameter_group_member tables

This step creates two related tables. `parameter_group` stores one row per group, while `parameter_group_member` links each group to its parameter IDs. Together, they represent the many-to-many relationship between parameters and groups.

```{r}
# Create the parameter-group lookup table
group_names <- sort(unique(parameter_group_candidates$group_name))

parameter_group <- data.frame(
  group_id = seq_along(group_names),
  group_name = group_names,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Create the table linking parameter IDs to groups
parameter_group_member <- unique(
  parameter_group_candidates[c("parameter_id", "group_name")]
)

parameter_group_member$group_id <- parameter_group$group_id[
  match(parameter_group_member$group_name, parameter_group$group_name)
]

parameter_group_member <- parameter_group_member[
  c("group_id", "parameter_id")
]

parameter_group_member <- parameter_group_member[
  order(parameter_group_member$group_id, parameter_group_member$parameter_id),
]

rownames(parameter_group_member) <- NULL

# Check that every parameter ID exists in the parameter catalogue
sum(!parameter_group_member$parameter_id %in% parameter_catalog$parameter_id)

View(parameter_group)
View(parameter_group_member)
```

### Standardise column names and inspect tables

This step renames parameter-description fields to match the SOP and changes the chromosome 2 column names into simpler names suitable for database use. It then prints the row counts and column names of the main tables so their structures can be checked before database creation.

```{r}
### Standardise database column names

#This step aligns the parameter fields with the SOP names and gives the chromosome 2 fields simple names that are convenient to use in SQL.

# Rename parameter fields to match the SOP
if ("parameterId" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description) &&
    !("parameter_id" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description))) {
  names(IMPC_parameter_description)[
    names(IMPC_parameter_description) == "parameterId"
  ] <- "parameter_id"
}

if ("name" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description) &&
    !("parameter_name" %in% names(IMPC_parameter_description))) {
  names(IMPC_parameter_description)[
    names(IMPC_parameter_description) == "name"
  ] <- "parameter_name"
}

# Rename chromosome 2 fields
old_names <- c(
  "Gene stable ID",
  "Transcript stable ID",
  "Gene name",
  "Exon stable ID",
  "Exon region start (bp)",
  "Exon region end (bp)",
  "Exon rank in transcript"
)

new_names <- c(
  "gene_stable_id",
  "transcript_stable_id",
  "gene_symbol",
  "exon_stable_id",
  "exon_start_bp",
  "exon_end_bp",
  "exon_rank"
)

for (i in seq_along(old_names)) {
  if (old_names[i] %in% names(chrom2) &&
      !(new_names[i] %in% names(chrom2))) {
    names(chrom2)[names(chrom2) == old_names[i]] <- new_names[i]
  }
}

# Check the column names
names(IMPC_parameter_description)
names(IMPC_procedure)
names(chrom2)




tables_to_check <- c(
  "clean_wide_data",
  "IMPC_parameter_description",
  "IMPC_procedure",
  "bespokeTask",
  "Disease_information",
  "chrom2",
  "parameter_group",
  "parameter_group_member"
)

for (table_name in tables_to_check) {
  if (exists(table_name) && is.data.frame(get(table_name))) {
    x <- get(table_name)
    cat(
      "\nTable:", table_name,
      "| Rows:", nrow(x),
      "| Columns:", ncol(x), "\n"
    )
    print(names(x))
  } else {
    cat("\nTable not found in R:", table_name, "\n")
  }
}
```

## Create the mouse_gene table

This step collects mouse MGI accession IDs and gene symbols from the main results, bespoke task, and disease information tables. It creates one row per MGI ID. When an ID is associated with conflicting symbols, the symbol is left blank for review instead of choosing one automatically.

```{r}
# Combine mouse gene IDs and symbols from the three tables
gene_source <- rbind(
  clean_wide_data[c("gene_accession_id", "gene_symbol")],
  bespokeTask[c("gene_accession_id", "gene_symbol")],
  Disease_information[c("gene_accession_id", "gene_symbol")]
)

gene_source$gene_accession_id <- trimws(
  as.character(gene_source$gene_accession_id)
)
gene_source$gene_symbol <- trimws(
  as.character(gene_source$gene_symbol)
)

# Keep rows with an MGI ID
gene_source <- gene_source[
  !is.na(gene_source$gene_accession_id) &
    gene_source$gene_accession_id != "",
]

# Create one row for every MGI ID, including IDs with no symbol
gene_ids <- unique(gene_source$gene_accession_id)

mouse_gene <- data.frame(
  gene_accession_id = gene_ids,
  gene_symbol = NA_character_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Assign a symbol only when the ID has exactly one unambiguous symbol
for (i in seq_along(gene_ids)) {
  symbols <- unique(
    gene_source$gene_symbol[
      gene_source$gene_accession_id == gene_ids[i] &
        !is.na(gene_source$gene_symbol) &
        gene_source$gene_symbol != ""
    ]
  )

  if (length(symbols) == 1) {
    mouse_gene$gene_symbol[i] <- symbols
  }
}

View(mouse_gene)
```

### Create the SQL database schema

#first version

The database is organised around the identifiers shared by the data. mouse_gene provides one record for each MGI gene accession ID and links the mouse gene data in clean_wide_data, bespokeTask, and Disease_information. clean_wide_data also links to IMPC_parameter_description through parameter_id. IMPC_procedure links to the parameter description table through impcParameterOrigId, while parameter_group_member links parameters to their groups.

chrom2 is stored as a separate table. It identifies genes using Ensembl gene_stable_id, whereas the other mouse gene tables use MGI gene_accession_id. Since the supplied data does not include a verified mapping between these identifiers, no relationship was created between chrom2 and the other tables. Its transcript and exon records remain available for queries using the Ensembl IDs and gene symbols in chrom2.

```{sql connection=}
CREATE TABLE mouse_gene (
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    PRIMARY KEY (gene_accession_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE IMPC_parameter_description (
    parameter_id VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    impcParameterOrigId VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    parameter_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (parameter_id),
    UNIQUE (impcParameterOrigId)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE IMPC_procedure (
    procedure_id BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    isMandatory BOOLEAN,
    impcParameterOrigId VARCHAR(30),
    PRIMARY KEY (procedure_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (impcParameterOrigId)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description (impcParameterOrigId)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE parameter_group (
    group_id INT NOT NULL,
    group_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (group_id),
    UNIQUE (group_name)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE parameter_group_member (
    group_id INT NOT NULL,
    parameter_id VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (group_id, parameter_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (group_id)
        REFERENCES parameter_group (group_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (parameter_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description (parameter_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE clean_wide_data (
    result_id BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    source_file VARCHAR(30),
    analysis_id VARCHAR(12),
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(20),
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    allele_symbol VARCHAR(100),
    strain_name VARCHAR(100),
    parameter_id VARCHAR(30),
    pvalue DOUBLE,
    parameter_name VARCHAR(255),
    mouse_life_stage VARCHAR(30),
    lacz_blood VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_brain VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_colon VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_eye VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_heart VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_kidney VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_liver VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_lung VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_skeletal_muscle VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_skin VARCHAR(50),
    lacz_vascular_system VARCHAR(50),
    PRIMARY KEY (result_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene (gene_accession_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (parameter_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description (parameter_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE bespokeTask (
    bespoke_task_id BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    human_gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    human_entrez_gene_id VARCHAR(20),
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(20),
    high_level_mp_ids TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (bespoke_task_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene (gene_accession_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE Disease_information (
    disease_information_id BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    human_gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    human_gene_name VARCHAR(255),
    hgnc_id VARCHAR(20),
    do_term_name VARCHAR(255),
    do_term_id VARCHAR(20),
    mouse_genotype_ids TEXT,
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(20),
    PRIMARY KEY (disease_information_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene (gene_accession_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE chrom2 (
    chrom2_row_id BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    gene_stable_id VARCHAR(20),
    transcript_stable_id VARCHAR(20),
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(50),
    exon_stable_id VARCHAR(20),
    exon_start_bp BIGINT,
    exon_end_bp BIGINT,
    exon_rank INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (chrom2_row_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```


#final version

```{sql connection=}


-- ==============================================
-- IMPC DATABASE SCHEMA
-- 18 Tables
-- MySQL 8.0
-- ==============================================

-- 1. MOUSE GENE

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mouse_gene (
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY,
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),

    INDEX idx_mouse_symbol (gene_symbol)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 2. HUMAN GENE

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS human_gene (
    human_gene_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    human_gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),
    human_gene_name VARCHAR(255),
    human_entrez_gene_id VARCHAR(32),
    hgnc_id VARCHAR(32),

    INDEX idx_human_entrez (human_entrez_gene_id),
    INDEX idx_hgnc (hgnc_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 3. IMPC PARAMETER DESCRIPTION

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS IMPC_parameter_description (
    parameter_id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    impcParameterOrigId VARCHAR(64),
    parameter_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,

    INDEX idx_param_orig (impcParameterOrigId)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 4. IMPC PROCEDURE

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS IMPC_procedure (
    procedure_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    isMandatory BOOLEAN,
    impcParameterOrigId VARCHAR(64),

    INDEX idx_proc_orig (impcParameterOrigId)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 5. PROCEDURE-PARAMETER RELATIONSHIP

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS IMPC_procedure_parameter (
    procedure_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    parameter_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,

    PRIMARY KEY (procedure_id, parameter_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_ipp_procedure
        FOREIGN KEY (procedure_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_procedure(procedure_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_ipp_parameter
        FOREIGN KEY (parameter_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description(parameter_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 6. PARAMETER GROUP

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS parameter_group (
    group_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    group_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL UNIQUE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 7. PARAMETER GROUP MEMBER

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS parameter_group_member (
    group_id INT NOT NULL,
    parameter_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,

    PRIMARY KEY (group_id, parameter_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_pgm_group
        FOREIGN KEY (group_id)
        REFERENCES parameter_group(group_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_pgm_parameter
        FOREIGN KEY (parameter_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description(parameter_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 8. CLEAN WIDE DATA

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clean_wide_data (
    result_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,

    source_file VARCHAR(255),
    analysis_id VARCHAR(128),

    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(32),
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),

    allele_symbol VARCHAR(128),
    strain_name VARCHAR(128),
    mouse_life_stage VARCHAR(64),

    parameter_id VARCHAR(64),
    parameter_name VARCHAR(255),
    pvalue DOUBLE,

    CONSTRAINT fk_cwd_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene(gene_accession_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_cwd_parameter
        FOREIGN KEY (parameter_id)
        REFERENCES IMPC_parameter_description(parameter_id),

    CONSTRAINT chk_pvalue
        CHECK (
            pvalue IS NULL
            OR (pvalue >= 0 AND pvalue <= 1)
        ),

    INDEX idx_result_analysis (analysis_id),
    INDEX idx_result_gene (gene_accession_id),
    INDEX idx_result_parameter (parameter_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 9. LACZ EXPRESSION

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lacz_expression (
    result_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,

    lacz_blood VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_brain VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_colon VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_eye VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_heart VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_kidney VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_liver VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_lung VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_skeletal_muscle VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_skin VARCHAR(64),
    lacz_vascular_system VARCHAR(64),

    CONSTRAINT fk_lacz_result
        FOREIGN KEY (result_id)
        REFERENCES clean_wide_data(result_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 10. BESPOKE TASK

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bespokeTask (
    bespoke_task_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,

    human_gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),
    human_entrez_gene_id VARCHAR(32),

    gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(32),

    high_level_mp_ids TEXT,
    human_gene_id BIGINT,

    CONSTRAINT fk_bespoke_mouse_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene(gene_accession_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_bespoke_human_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (human_gene_id)
        REFERENCES human_gene(human_gene_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 11. MAMMALIAN PHENOTYPE TERMS

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mp_terms (
    mp_term_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY,
    mp_term_name VARCHAR(255)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 12. BESPOKE-MP RELATIONSHIP

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bespokeTask_mp (
    bespoke_task_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    mp_term_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,

    PRIMARY KEY (bespoke_task_id, mp_term_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_bmp_bespoke
        FOREIGN KEY (bespoke_task_id)
        REFERENCES bespokeTask(bespoke_task_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_bmp_mp
        FOREIGN KEY (mp_term_id)
        REFERENCES mp_terms(mp_term_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 13. HUMAN DISEASES

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS human_diseases (
    do_term_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY,
    do_term_name VARCHAR(255)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 14. DISEASE INFORMATION

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Disease_information (
    disease_information_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,

    human_gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),
    human_gene_name VARCHAR(255),
    hgnc_id VARCHAR(32),

    do_term_name VARCHAR(255),
    do_term_id VARCHAR(32),

    mouse_genotype_ids TEXT,

    gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),
    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(32),
    human_gene_id BIGINT,

    CONSTRAINT fk_disease_mouse_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene(gene_accession_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_disease_human_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (human_gene_id)
        REFERENCES human_gene(human_gene_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_disease_ontology
        FOREIGN KEY (do_term_id)
        REFERENCES human_diseases(do_term_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 15. DISEASE INFORMATION-GENOTYPE

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Disease_information_genotype (
    disease_information_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    mouse_genotype_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

    PRIMARY KEY (
        disease_information_id,
        mouse_genotype_id
    ),

    CONSTRAINT fk_dig_disease
        FOREIGN KEY (disease_information_id)
        REFERENCES Disease_information(disease_information_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 16. CHROMOSOME 2 TRANSCRIPT

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chrom2_transcript (
    transcript_stable_id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    gene_stable_id VARCHAR(64),
    gene_symbol VARCHAR(64),

    INDEX idx_chrom2_gene_stable (gene_stable_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 17. CHROMOSOME 2 EXON RECORDS

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chrom2 (
    chrom2_row_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,

    transcript_stable_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    exon_stable_id VARCHAR(64),

    exon_start_bp BIGINT,
    exon_end_bp BIGINT,
    exon_rank INT,

    CONSTRAINT fk_chrom2_transcript
        FOREIGN KEY (transcript_stable_id)
        REFERENCES chrom2_transcript(transcript_stable_id),

    INDEX idx_chrom2_exon (exon_stable_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;


-- 18. PARAMETER GROUP EXTERNAL DATA

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS parameter_group_external_data (
    external_record_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,

    group_id INT NOT NULL,

    resource_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    external_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,

    term_or_label VARCHAR(255),
    notes TEXT,

    gene_accession_id VARCHAR(32),

    CONSTRAINT fk_external_group
        FOREIGN KEY (group_id)
        REFERENCES parameter_group(group_id),

    CONSTRAINT fk_external_gene
        FOREIGN KEY (gene_accession_id)
        REFERENCES mouse_gene(gene_accession_id),

    INDEX idx_external_group (group_id, resource_name),
    INDEX idx_external_id (external_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;
```
